answer: Water bodies were identified via radar using a VV polarization threshold of -16.0 dB, which detected 5,511 water pixels (8.4% of the scene) in the SAR read tool. The optical water mask from the water_highlight tool detected 10,998 pixels (16.8% of the scene), but the two masks disagree with an IoU of only 0.012. The radar-derived water mask is more conservative, likely due to the radar’s sensitivity to surface roughness and the applied 3x3 boxcar smoothing. The SDWI metric, though reported, was not used for the water mask. The water pixels are distributed across the scene, with higher concentrations in the southern and central regions where darker, smoother patches appear in the radar image.
